name: Haiti
summary: The revolution that broke the plantation empire.
notes: The western part of Hispaniola is tracked separately from the east. Spanish and British incursions during the revolution held parts of the territory; they did not replace French rule everywhere. Indigenous communities and descendants survived conquest.

events.title: Spain claims Hispaniola
events.detail: Columbus asserted a Spanish claim to an inhabited island.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Spanish colonial foothold
events.detail: La Navidad’s destruction was followed by a renewed Spanish colonizing expedition. Rule spread violently and unevenly.
events.uncertainty: The western track summarizes the early Hispaniola colony; this is not a date of complete territorial conquest.

events.title: A fractured western frontier
events.detail: French and English buccaneers established bases around Tortuga while Spain claimed the island.
events.uncertainty: Settlement was gradual; no single handover date.

events.title: French colonial administration
events.detail: France brought western settlements into its colonial system.

events.title: Ryswick recognizes the division
events.detail: The peace settlement is conventionally used to mark recognition of French Saint-Domingue in the west.
events.uncertainty: Recognition consolidated an existing colonial foothold; the modern border was not drawn in 1697.

events.title: Enslaved people rise in revolution
events.detail: A mass uprising began the struggle that would overthrow slavery and colonial rule.

events.title: A war on several fronts
events.detail: Spanish and British forces intervened as revolutionary armies fought for freedom and power.

events.title: Toussaint’s autonomous constitution
events.detail: Louverture governed under nominal French sovereignty; autonomy was not yet Haitian independence.

events.title: Napoleon sends an expedition
events.detail: France attempted to reassert metropolitan control; resistance defeated the expedition.

events.title: Haiti declares independence
events.detail: The revolution defeated France and created an independent state founded on the abolition of slavery.

events.title: U.S. occupation begins
events.detail: U.S. Marines landed after a presidential assassination; military and financial control followed without annexation.

events.title: The occupation ends
events.detail: The last U.S. Marines left; foreign financial oversight outlasted military occupation.
